language.secondary: four loop bars round a court; the north and east bars tall at four storeys, the south and west bars low at step 0.55 - two dominant arms crossing at the NE corner read as the structural event
language.formal_principle: r2 diagnosis round 2: split-then-shear produced a silent word (split along 'long' on this parcel returns empty geometry at ratio 0.50 - the silence gate refused both halves). New principle: a loop with narrow bars already places four arms that physically cross at the corners; differentiate with step so bar_s and bar_w become low podiums (55% height) and bar_n and bar_e remain tall - the two tall arms crossing at the NE corner are the two-bar event the original sentence wanted. No interlock, no split, no rubble. The short bars hold the ground at grade; the tall pair is the silhouette.

language.secondary: a four-storey bar compressed to a genuine spine; four one-storey lateral branches grow from its long flanks at grade
language.formal_principle: r2 sheet diagnosis: branch delivered one visible stub because the trunk was a square extrude with no long flanks - the branch op could not find four eligible sides to grip. Fix: compress the trunk toward 'e' after extrude so the body narrows east-west and becomes a true north-south bar whose long east and west faces give the branch op clear extended flanks. The compress ratio 0.62 is the minimum allowed (0.6 floor) rounded up one notch for gate safety, producing a genuine 3:2 bar from a square base. Branches then grow eastward and westward from the long flanks at grade.

language.secondary: a one-podium, one-house building: a deep ground plate holding the hall, and a two-storey gabled bar riding it - the house is the building, only its ground is ceded
language.formal_principle: The 210 m2 hall wants a deep flat plate and the dwelling-scaled rooms want a house section, and neither survives inside the other - so they stratify: the hall takes the entire ground as a podium plate, and the house, a two-storey bar under one ridge, rides on top; the gable is not a crown on a pile, it is most of the building, standing one storey above the street it gave its ground to.

gap.basis: widest band-level narrowest component separation; not verified circulation
